\caption{\textbf{Unit representations compared at matched numbers of tests.} Stage-1 units and the broader units produced by Stage 2 on all chromosomes were each represented in six ways and tested genome-wide. In each partition, the minimum unit size was raised until about 100 units remained, and units spanning more than 1 Mb were excluded. Min-$p$ uses the phenotype to choose the member with the smallest p-value and is therefore an optimistic reference, not a valid test; the random member is a chance baseline. For the highest-$\ldw$ and central members, Median rank/$n$ gives the median rank of the chosen member's p-value within its unit (1 = smallest) and the median unit size. The highest-$\ldw$ and central-member Min. $p$ values are identical in the two partitions because the same Chr5 region (2.48--2.50 Mb) was the top unit in both and the same member was chosen; the random-member values agree only to three significant figures. Regions: significant units assembled into outlier regions with the same Stage-2 rule as in the main analysis.}\label{tab:goldilocks-units}\\
